```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Read the extracted data for the name Andrew
andrew_data <- read_csv("Andrew.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Male Andrews Over the Years

```{r}
#| label: male-andrews-plot
# Filter for male Andrews
male_andrews <- andrew_data |>
  filter(sex == "M")

# Significant historical data points with context
male_events <- tibble(
  year = c(1960, 1987, 1993),
  n = c(8201, 36206, 27326),
  label = c(
    "1960 Spike: Birth of UK Prince Andrew",
    "1987 Peak: Royal wedding & 80s pop culture",
    "1993 Dip: Post-Hurricane Andrew (1992)"
  )
)

# Plot line, points, and descriptive labels
p_male <- ggplot(male_andrews, aes(x = year, y = n)) +
  geom_line(color = "#1f78b4", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = male_events, aes(x = year, y = n), color = "#e31a1c", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = male_events,
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = label),
    vjust = -1,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Popularity of the Name Andrew (Males)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Wrap in ggplotly to enable interactive hover values
ggplotly(p_male)
```

## Female Andrews

```{r}
#| label: female-andrews-plot
# Filter for female Andrews
female_andrews <- andrew_data |>
  filter(sex == "F")

# Peak year for female Andrews
female_events <- tibble(
  year = 1987,
  n = 223,
  label = "1987 Peak: Andrew mania spilled into female names!"
)

# Plot female Andrews with peak label
p_female <- ggplot(female_andrews, aes(x = year, y = n)) +
  geom_line(color = "#e7298a", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = female_events, aes(x = year, y = n), color = "#7570b3", size = 2.5) +
  geom_text(
    data = female_events,
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = label),
    vjust = -1,
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Yes there are female andrews too",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of Babies"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Wrap in ggplotly to enable interactive hover values
ggplotly(p_female)
```
